provenance.note: Curated compilation - per-record citations (HYDRAA, HMDA, MRDCL, dated press) carry the accountability.

note: Active water-restoration programmes for Hyderabad. Every entry is reshaped from an already-verified commitment in commitments-hyderabad.json and carries that entry's source, so the two surfaces cannot drift apart. Hyderabad's restoration programmes are unusually hard to hold to account: most are announced without a dated deliverable, which is why several statuses read as a stated intent rather than a measured position. The one exception is the FTL notification programme, which is continuously auditable because the promising authority publishes the register that records it.

projects.operator: Musi Riverfront Development Corporation / Government of Telangana
projects.scope: Rejuvenation of a 55 km stretch of the Musi from Gandipet to Gowrelly. The single largest intervention on the river, and the hardest to track: no dated deliverable has been published against it.
projects.funding_summary: Rs 375 crore released in May 2026 as the first instalment against Rs 1,500 crore earmarked in the 2026-27 state budget (commitment id: musi-riverfront-phase1)
projects.status: In progress (first instalment released May 2026); no dated milestone published.

projects.scheme_name: Musi sewage interception and diversion, Bapu Ghat to Gowrelly
projects.scope: Interception and diversion of sewage outfalls before they reach the river along a 34 km reach. This is the load-bearing claim in every Musi cleanup plan: without interception, riverfront construction changes the bank rather than the water.
projects.funding_summary: Sewage-side counterpart to the riverfront works (commitment id: musi-sewage-interception)
projects.status: Announced; the trapped-outfall count is not reported, so progress is not auditable. Delhi's equivalent - trapping 39 drains to the Yamuna - is trackable because the trapped count is published.

projects.scheme_name: 39 sewage treatment plants along the Musi under AMRUT
projects.operator: HMWSSB, under the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation
projects.scope: 39 STPs totalling a reported 972 MLD, on top of an existing estate and a further tranche described as already commissioned.
projects.status: Sanctioned under AMRUT 2.0: '39 STPs with a capacity of 972 million litres per day (MLD)' at Rs 3,849.10 crore, in HMWSSB's press release reported by Siasat on 4 Sep 2025. The Government of Telangana's NGT filing (OA 606/2018) gives '36 STPs of capacity 1435.30 MLD' in operation in GHMC as on 31.12.2024. The two count different sets of plants, so this site quotes each as printed and does not add them into one treatment-capacity number.

projects.operator: Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA)
projects.scope: A stated target of ten lake restorations a year against a vision of 200 restored lakes. Six lakes were taken up in a first phase and 14 more are to be restored in a second, and restoration of four more began on 25 June 2026 with bhoomi puja at Ibrahim Pedda Cheruvu (Rajendranagar), Bhagirathamma Cheruvu (Gandipet), Kamuni Cheruvu (Moosapet) and Kapra Cheruvu (Medchal-Malkajgiri).
projects.funding_summary: State programme; per-lake cost not published (commitment id: hydraa-lake-restoration)
projects.status: Ten a year is a stated target, not a measured rate: we have not found a count of lakes completed each year to set against it. The Week reports a vision of '200 rejuvenated lakes across Hyderabad within a decade'; the metropolitan register holds 2,978 lakes.

projects.scheme_name: Gazetted Full Tank Level final notifications
projects.scope: Every lake in the register is meant to receive a preliminary FTL notification and then a final one after objections are heard. Until the final notification issues, the boundary is not legally settled and there is nothing definite to prosecute encroachment against.
projects.funding_summary: Statutory process, not a funded scheme (commitment id: ftl-final-notifications)
projects.status: 1,352 of 2,978 lakes final-notified (45.4%); 1,626 still carry only a preliminary notification. Near-dormant from 2017 to 2023, then 533 in 2024 and 533 in 2025. Rangareddy is the laggard at 34.5%.

_court_orders_note: Deliberately empty. Hyderabad has substantial lake and Musi litigation, but no case citation has been verified to this file's standard (court, case number, date, order text or a primary report of it). Delhi's equivalent list carries six because each was traced to an NGT or High Court document. Inventing or half-citing a case here would be worse than an empty array; this is a named gap, not an absence of litigation.
